intro: If you've been thinking about converting a tired bathroom into a sleek, accessible wet room, you're not alone — it's one of the most popular bathroom upgrades we see homeowners in Ely requesting right now. Whether you're planning ahead for later life, want to add genuine value to your home, or simply fancy a luxurious, spa-like space, a professionally installed wet room delivers on all fronts. Done properly, it's a watertight, low-maintenance solution that works beautifully in everything from a compact ensuite to a generous family bathroom. The key word there is properly — wet room installation is one of those jobs where cutting corners early leads to expensive problems later.
localContext: Ely's housing stock is wonderfully varied, and that variety has a real impact on how wet room installations are planned and priced. Older stone-built properties and period cottages — particularly those found closer to the cathedral and along the older streets of the city — often have solid floors, uneven subfloors, or original timber joists that need careful assessment before any tanking work begins. Modern estates on the edges of Ely tend to be more straightforward, with standard timber or concrete floors that follow predictable construction methods. That said, even newer builds can have quirks. One factor that affects every Ely home equally is the moderately hard water supply in this part of Cambridgeshire. Hard water accelerates limescale build-up on screens, drains, and fixtures, so it's worth factoring in a water softener or at least specifying fittings with good scale resistance when planning your wet room. A local installer who knows the area will raise this with you automatically — it's the kind of detail that makes a real difference long-term.
serviceDetail: A wet room installation is more involved than a standard shower enclosure replacement, and understanding the process helps you plan realistically. The first step is a proper survey of the existing bathroom — assessing the floor structure, drainage options, and wall construction. In older Ely properties, this stage sometimes uncovers issues like inadequate joist depth or outdated pipework that need addressing before the wet room work begins. Once the survey is complete and a design agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped back to a shell. The floor is then prepared and a former or screed is laid to create the correct fall towards the drain — typically around 1 in 80 — so water flows away efficiently rather than pooling. Tanking comes next: a fully waterproof membrane is applied to the floor and at least 1.8 metres up the walls, with particular attention to corners and pipe penetrations where leaks most commonly occur. This is the most critical stage of the whole job. Once the tanking is cured and tested, tiling, fitting the linear or point drain, and installing the shower valve and screen can proceed. Final fixes include installing lighting, ventilation (essential in a wet room environment), and any heated towel rails or underfloor heating. From start to finish, most installations in Ely take between five and eight working days depending on the complexity of the space.
pricing: Wet room installation in Ely typically falls in the range of £6,000 to £12,000 for a complete project, including labour and materials. At the lower end you're looking at a straightforward installation in a modern property with standard tiling and a mid-range drain and valve. Costs rise with the complexity of the property — older stone-built homes and period cottages in Ely often require additional structural preparation, rerouting of pipework, or bespoke solutions to work around uneven floors. Premium tile choices, designer drains, frameless glass screens, underfloor heating, and high-spec shower systems can add £1,500 to £3,000 on top of the base cost. Always get a detailed, itemised quote before committing.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who works regularly in Ely genuinely matters for a project like this. They'll be familiar with the common construction methods used in local period properties, know which suppliers nearby stock the materials needed, and won't be padding a quote to cover unfamiliar travel. A local installer is also far easier to get back if any snagging needs attention after completion — and on a job as technical as wet room tanking, that peace of mind is worth a great deal. Word-of-mouth reputation matters in a town the size of Ely, and tradespeople who work here regularly have every reason to get it right.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older Ely property with timber floors?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires careful preparation. Timber joists need to be assessed for depth and condition, and a suitable decoupling board or reinforced screed must be used before tanking begins. It's more involved than a concrete floor installation, and a good installer in Ely will survey this thoroughly before quoting. Skipping this step is what leads to leaks and costly remedial work further down the line.

faqs.q: How do I protect a wet room from limescale given Ely's hard water supply?
faqs.a: Ely sits in a moderately hard water area, so limescale on drains, screens, and fittings is a genuine consideration. Specifying fittings with limescale-resistant coatings helps, as does installing an inline water softener or descaler unit. A squeegee after each use makes a surprising difference to screen longevity too. Raise this with your installer at the design stage rather than as an afterthought.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Ely?
faqs.a: Most wet room projects in Ely take between five and eight working days, though older or more complex properties can extend this to ten days or more. The tanking stage requires curing time before tiling can proceed, so there's an unavoidable pause mid-project. Your installer should give you a realistic day-by-day schedule before work begins so you can plan around having the bathroom out of use.

faqs.q: Does a wet room add value to a home in Ely?
faqs.a: A well-executed wet room can certainly add appeal and value, particularly in family homes and properties marketed to buyers who are thinking about long-term accessibility. In Ely's mix of period cottages and modern estate homes, a high-quality wet room is increasingly seen as a premium feature rather than a niche adaptation. The key is quality of installation — a poorly tanked wet room that's leaked behind tiles is a liability, not an asset.
